text:
maria-support: New onboarding for NovusAI — customer says API key was created but calls return 403, console shows key under 'org-default' instead of their project. Can someone take?
eli-cs: on it. do we have the provisioner logs? tenant id + project id from customer?
maria-support: tenant=tn-novus-234, project=novus-prod, sample curl they ran: `curl -H \"Authorization: Bearer sk-live-XXXXXXXX\" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/models` -> 403
ben-oncall: @maria-support please paste the full response body (403) and the key id visible in console. quick check: sometimes OIDC claim race leaves key visible but unbound.
maria-support: response body: `{\n  \"error\": \"permission_denied\",\n  \"message\": \"service account not authorized for project: novus-prod\"\n}` key id in console: key_3a9f2b
sam-devops: provisioning trace shows key_3a9f2b created at 3335001090 by provisioner-v2, but binder job for project binding ran at 3335001300 — looks like bind happened ~200s later. customer tried keys during that window.
eli-cs: aha intermittent window. any evidence it was created in a different org first?
sam-devops: yes, the create event shows parent_org=internal-tools (partner org) then later reparented to tn-novus-234. Provisioner retried path: `POST /internal/provision -> createKey(key_3a9f2b) -> queue bind` then reparent job executed. Reparenting reproduces console visibility earlier than IAM policy sync.
maria-support: timeline we can send to customer? they want root cause for production access being blocked.
ben-oncall: timeline: create 3335001090 -> key visible in console 3335001096 -> customer tried call 3335001105 -> 403 -> binder job ran 3335001300 -> bind completed 3335001310 -> calls succeeded 3335001320.
deploy-bot: [deploy-log] provisioner-v2: create(key_3a9f2b) -> idempotent_create ok
eli-cs: repro steps to validate: 1) create new tenant via onboarding API 2) simulate provisioner delayed bind with `--force-visibility` flag to surface key early 3) attempt API call before binder runs -> expect 403
eli-cs: command (internal):
```
curl -X POST https://internal-api.redwood.local/onboard \
  -d '{"tenant":"tn-test-xyz","project":"proj-test"}' \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $PROVISIONER_TOKEN'
# then read create event from provisioner logs
```
sam-devops: mitigation for NovusAI: manually rebind and rotate key to be safe, but since bind completed, they can continue. I recommend we rotate the key and ensure binder has completed before they go live.
maria-support: did rotation for them and confirmed calls now return 200. customer notified.
ben-oncall: follow-up actions: 1) add a health check that prevents surface-visible keys until bind_confirm event 2) emit metric `provision.binding_latency` and alert on >30s 3) add a note in onboarding docs about potential short window where calls return 403.
eli-cs: agreed. I'll open a tiny runbook PR to block visibility and another to add the metric.
maria-support: FYI ticket #SUP-5421 created with logs and timeline for NovusAI; customer updated that they're unblocked. :thumbsup:
ben-oncall: thanks. tagging @sam-devops for postmortem and followup on binder SLA.
sam-devops: noted, will include repro and patch timeline. planning patch to ensure bind is synchronous for initial key until we have async guarantees.
maria-support: closing thread once PR and metric exist. thanks all.
